An imaginary creature with serrated horns, somewhat similar to the heraldic antelope.
Any of various long-legged wading birds in the family Threskiornithidae, having long downcurved bills used to probe the mud for prey such as crustaceans.
A peninsula and region of Europe south of the Pyrenees, consisting of Andorra, Spain, Portugal, and Gibraltar.
A city and town in Missouri.
A census-designated place in Ohio.

An antique and Byzantine name for the geographic region and ancient Georgian kingdom of Kartli in Eastern Europe, located east of Colchis, corresponding roughly to the eastern parts of present-day Georgia.
Native to Iberia.
Of or pertaining to Iberia.

An ancient people settled in the eastern and southern coasts of the Iberian Peninsula, at least from the 6th century BCE.
A Georgian (person from the country in Eurasia).
A synthetic compound used widely as an analgesic and anti-inflammatory drug.

An island of the Balearic Islands, Spain.
A city and municipality of Ibiza.
Any member of the species Lynx pardinus of endangered lynxes, native to the Iberian peninsula.
Of, from or relating to the island of Ibiza, Balearic Islands, Spain.

A peninsula located in the extreme southwest of Europe which includes modern day Spain, Portugal, Andorra and Gibraltar, bordered on the south and east by the Mediterranean Sea, and on the north and west by the Atlantic Ocean, with the Pyrenees forming the northeast edge of the peninsula, connecting it to the rest of Europe.
Ibidorhyncha struthersii, a species of wading bird inhabiting the shingle riverbanks of the high plateau of Central Asia and the Himalayas.

The doctrines associated with Ibadis, such as the acceptance of fewer hadiths, and the addition of Jami Sahih as a canonical hadith.

Phylloscopus ibericus, a species of leaf warbler endemic to Portugal, Spain and North Africa, west of a line stretching roughly from the western Pyrenees via the mountains of central Spain to the Atlantic.
